title: Limit on the Rise of the Installment for Assisted Patients by Insurance Status
content:
Financial-assistance coordination standard — **Patient Payment Plans**: the most the regular installment may rise when an invoice is added, for patients with an award under the Patient Financial Assistance Program, according to whether insurance is on file under Insurance Coverage & Claims.

## The rule

The cap on the rise depends on the award and the coverage: for a patient with an approved financial-assistance award and a live insurance coverage on file, the added-invoice installment is never more than double the installment standing on the plan; for a patient with an approved award and no live coverage, never more than 75 percent above it; for any other patient, never more than 25 percent above it.

When the installment worked out is higher than the cap, the added-invoice installment is the standing installment raised by the capped percentage, rounded to the nearest cent with an exact half cent rounded up, and the plan runs on until its balance is cleared.

## Reading the records

- **Approved award** — a case of the patient under the Patient Financial Assistance Program whose status is approved.
- **Live insurance coverage on file** — a coverage of the patient under Insurance Coverage & Claims whose status is active.

## Cap by award and coverage

| Approved award | Live coverage on file | Most the installment may rise | Ceiling on a standing installment of 120.00 (hypothetical) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 100 percent (double) | 240.00 |
| Yes | No | 75 percent | 210.00 |
| No | Yes or No | 25 percent | 150.00 |

## Hypothetical cases (standing installment 120.00; installment worked out 187.14)

- Approved award and an active Medicare Advantage Plan coverage: the ceiling is 240.00, so 187.14 stands.
- Approved award, no active coverage: the ceiling is 210.00, so 187.14 stands.
- No approved award: the ceiling is 150.00, so the added-invoice installment is 150.00 and the plan runs on until its balance is cleared.
